name: Wyoming
summary: Statutes: the Legislative Service Office publishes the whole Wyoming Statutes as one PDF per title at wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/TitleNN.pdf (constructible from the citation; fetch_doc.py reads them in full; the fetch tool is gated for these built URLs); wyoleg.gov itself is an Angular app whose HTML pages are empty to both tools, and the LSO disclaims official status. Justia (2025) is a constructible tier-2 fallback per section. Constitution: Title97.pdf on the same path, Justia one-page fallback. Court rules: full-set PDFs on wyocourts.gov (Civil Procedure, Criminal Procedure and Appellate Procedure are large annotated LexisNexis-produced pamphlets: corpus candidates). Case law: the Supreme Court is the only appellate court and has used public-domain citations ('2024 WY 138') since 2001; the official opinions list (2006 on) is a JavaScript table neither tool can read, so Justia (1870-2026, cases.justia.com PDFs readable by script) is the practical route. Admin code: rules.wyo.gov is an ASP.NET search with no permalinks; Cornell LII mirrors it per section.

citation_map.notes: Statute numbers are TITLE-CHAPTER-SECTION (1-3-105, 6-2-101); the title number alone picks the PDF (Title01.pdf … Title42.pdf; constitution = Title97.pdf). The hundreds digit of the section is the article within a chapter that has articles (6-2-101 = ch. 2, art. 1); Justia inserts /article-N/ only for such chapters. A range 'W.S. 16-3-101 through 115' or '§§ 1-1-101 - 1-1-105' is a span: the regex takes the first section only. 'W.S.' is the LSO's own short form (often 'W.S. 1977'); it is guarded so it does not fire inside other abbreviations. Constitution articles are Arabic in the official text ('Article 1, Section 8'); Roman numerals also accepted. Wyoming has had a public-domain citation since 2001 ('YYYY WY N', paragraph pinpoints '¶ N'); Bluebook form adds P.3d and '(Wyo. YYYY)'. The official Wyoming Reports ended in 1959 (vol. 80, from memory); bare 'NN Wyo. NNN' is that reporter. Docket numbers: S-YY-NNNN (civil/criminal appeals), D-YY-NNNN (attorney discipline); before about 2010 dockets were bare 'NN-NNN' (e.g. 06-20), too generic to route. There is no intermediate appellate court. Court-rule abbreviations follow the courts' own annotated pamphlets (W.R.C.P., W.R.Cr.P., W.R.A.P., W.R.E., U.R.D.C.); circuit-court civil rules (W.R.C.P.C.C.) are deliberately NOT matched by the W.R.C.P. pattern. The agency.program.chapter admin-code form is inferred from the Secretary of State's description of its numbering (agency, program, chapter, effective date) and was not seen in a real citation: treat as unverified. CourtListener id 'wyo' from memory, unverified. law_aliases map short forms to the source id or PDF key that serves them. Fix 2026-10-17: singular 'Wyoming Statute §' and prose 'Article I, § 6 of the Wyoming Constitution' added after the independent regex test.

sources.title: Wyoming Statutes — per-title PDFs (Legislative Service Office)
sources.official_status_evidence: LSO disclaimer (wyoleg.gov/Legislature/disclaimer, JavaScript-rendered; text read from the site's app bundle): site information 'is not the official record' of the Legislature and is subject to revision. The annotated Wyoming Statutes are published by LexisNexis.
sources.coverage: All titles 1-42 of the Wyoming Statutes, text only (no annotations), one PDF per title; Title97 = Wyoming Constitution.

access.pattern_rules: title = the first number of the citation, zero-padded to 2 digits (W.S. 1-3-105 → Title01.pdf; 6-2-101 → Title06.pdf; 27-14-102 → Title27.pdf). The path is case-insensitive (IIS): /Statutes/compress/title01.pdf returns the same file. Inside the PDF each section starts with a heading line '{title}-{chapter}-{section}.   Catchline.' (e.g. '1-3-105. Actions other than recovery of real property.'); grep for '{cite}.' — the full stop after the number is what lands on the heading rather than on cross-references (grep strips trailing spaces). Missing files do NOT 404: wyoleg.gov returns the Angular app shell (HTTP 200, 0 text chars) for unknown paths — treat a 0-char 'html' result as not found.
access.navigation: The StatutesDownload page is a JavaScript app (empty to both tools); its list of 43 links (Constitution + Titles 1-42) is the url_pattern above.

automation.notes: WebFetch on Title01.pdf returned PROVENANCE_REQUIRED (built URL, permission not answered); not retried. fetch_doc.py reads whole titles (Title01: 366 pp, 730,731 chars; Title06: 210 pp, 407,091 chars) — far beyond the fetch tool's ~100K window, so the script or a corpus is the only full-text route. Section headings are indented with multiple spaces; fetch_doc.py grep normalises whitespace and strips trailing spaces — rely on the full stop. Title43.pdf (nonexistent) returns 0-char html.

currency.where: StatutesDownload page (JavaScript-rendered; read from the app bundle); the PDFs carry no currency line. HTTP Last-Modified on the PDFs: 8 May 2026.
currency.observed: reflects the contents of the statutes as they exist as of July 1, 2026.

access.pattern_rules: Agency/subagency/chapter pages are constructible from agency number (3 digits), program (4 digits) and chapter. Section URLs are NOT uniform: one chapter links sections under the chapter path (…/chapter-1/053-1-Wyo-Code-R-SSSS-1-1), another links them flat (…/regulations/wyoming/020-2-Wyo-Code-R-SSSS-2-1). Always take the section link from the chapter page. Section slugs come in -SSSS- and -SS- forms (015-1-Wyo-Code-R-SS-1-1 under agency-015/subagency-0001). The LII cite 'AAA-C Wyo. Code R. § C-S' omits the program/subagency and is ambiguous (015-1 … § 1-1 exists under both subagency-0001 and subagency-0008): identify the program from the citing context (agency division or rule title), else open agency-AAA and match the chapter TITLE against each subagency's chapter list; if still ambiguous, report both rather than guess.

access.pattern_rules: Recent years: case page = /{year}/{docket lower-case}.html (S-24-0162 → s-24-0162.html; discipline D-24-0005 → d-24-0005.html) and PDF = https://cases.justia.com/wyoming/supreme-court/{year}-{docket_lower}.pdf (the ?ts= query is optional). sources.coverage: No intermediate appellate court: district-court and chancery decisions go straight to the Supreme Court; its decisions are reviewed only on petition for rehearing (W.R.A.P. 9.08, within 15 days) or by U.S. Supreme Court certiorari.
